messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: New incident opened: serving-runtime errors + capacity churn impacting prod inference. Severity: P2. Autoscaler triggered repeated scale-ups/downs leading to pod crashloops and node flaps. Paging oncall anya (oncall).

anya (oncall): seeing repeated CUDA OOMs on inference pods, lots of restart_count spikes. Topline: latency + error rate up. Investigating now.

matthew: confirming — k8s events show flurry of scale events from hpa-controller -> nodes get added, then shortly evicted. Looks like rapid scale-out then immediate downscale.

eng-runtime-jay: sharing logs from a crashing pod:
```
I tensorflow/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_driver.cc:xxx] failed to allocate 104857600 bytes: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
2026-03-15T10:10:22Z runtime: kv-cache miss, attempting reinit
E runtime/serve: oom detected, killing process, exit code 137
```

ops-danielle: also seeing kubelet complaints about oom and pressure on GPUs. Node GPU memory fragmentation indicator high.

anya (oncall): quick questions - which autoscaler is that? HPA or custom external?

matthew: HPA driven by queue length + custom scaling policy from autoscale-controller v2. It has aggressive burst policy with 30s evaluation window.

eng-runtime-jay: hypothesis: bursty request spike -> autoscaler spikes replicas, new pods schedule on fresh nodes; initial warmup costs cause higher GPU memory usage (quant kernels + kv-cache warmup). Downscale triggers after short idle window -> pods get killed mid-warmup -> repeated churn -> memory fragmentation and CUDA OOMs.

product-eli: customer impact? Support?

support-bot: Ticket summary: ~120 customer requests delayed over 30m, ~3 broadly visible errors in client monitoring. No full-service outage but degraded. Support alerted customers on impacted orgs.

ops-danielle: immediate mitigations I'm going to try: 1) apply a cooldown to autoscaler (increase stabilizationWindow to 3m), 2) reduce maxReplicas from 150 -> 60 for this model route, 3) pin heavy models to smaller max_concurrency. Applying now.

eng-runtime-jay: also recommend enabling node-eviction backoff and bumping kube-scheduler conservative thresholds. Proposal: set HPA.behavior.scaleDown.stabilizationWindowSeconds=180 and behavior.scaleUp.stabilizationWindowSeconds=60.

anya (oncall): running kubectl apply to patch HPA:
```
kubectl -n prod patch hpa inference-v2 -p '{"spec":{"behavior":{"scaleDown":{"stabilizationWindowSeconds":180},"scaleUp":{"stabilizationWindowSeconds":60}}}}'
kubectl -n prod patch hpa inference-v2 -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":60}}'
```

incident-bot: HPA patched by anya (oncall) at 2026-03-15T10:18:11Z.

matthew: cordoning the most noisy nodes (gpu-node-7, gpu-node-9) to let pods reschedule more evenly.

ops-danielle: cordon + drain commands:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-7 && kubectl drain gpu-node-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

eng-runtime-jay: temporary runtime change: turned off aggressive kv-cache prefetch for the heavy model shard on that route to reduce memory footprint during warmup. That should help immediate OOMs while we stabilize autoscaler.

anya (oncall): after patches: crashloop backoff events down ~70%, restart rates dropping. Error rate falling from 8% -> 1.6% over 12m. Latency p95 still slightly elevated.

product-eli: good, keep me posted. I'll draft a short status note for affected customers with ETA for full recovery.

support-bot: customer notification sent to impacted orgs at 10:32Z.

matthew: one oddity — a subset of pods still show CUDA allocation failures during startup even after patch. Possible kernel-level memory fragmentation on a few nodes. I'll try a rolling restart of those nodes (drain -> reboot).

ops-danielle: scheduling reboots for gpu-node-3 and gpu-node-11 now, in small batches.

eng-runtime-jay: long-term: need to add scale-in cooldowns tied to model warmup metrics (e.g., kv-cache-ready) rather than pure idle time. Also consider reserve capacity for heavy models to avoid warmup thrash. Filing follow-up.

anya (oncall): reboots done for targeted nodes — pods moved to healthier nodes and stabilized. Crashloops down to baseline. Observability: token throughput recovered to expected range.

incident-bot: Incident moving to mitigated status at 2026-03-15T10:44:00Z.

anya (oncall): handing off to night oncall maya (night-oncall) for monitoring and postmortem follow-up. Summary for handoff:
- Root symptom: autoscaler reactive burst + short stabilization window caused rapid scale up/down -> pod warmup fragmentation -> CUDA OOMs and node pressure -> crashloops.
- Actions taken: increased HPA stabilization windows, lowered maxReplicas for route, cordoned/flushed noisy nodes, turned off kv-cache prefetch for heavy model, rebooted 2 nodes.
- Impact: degraded latency and ~120 delayed requests, ~3 visible client errors. No data loss. Support notified.
- Next steps assigned: eng-runtime to propose scale-in gating by warmup metric (ticket #INC-2480), infra to evaluate reserved capacity options for peak routes, SRE to draft postmortem.

maya (night-oncall): received, will watch for next 4h and consolidate logs for postmortem. If anything flips back to high error rate I'll escalate. Good work team. :thumbsup:

product-eli: please add customer-facing summary to the incident doc and tag me when ready.

incident-bot: participants updated: eng-runtime-jay, ops-danielle, anya (oncall), matthew, product-eli, support-bot, maya (night-oncall).

anya (oncall): adding quick runbook note: for model routes with heavy GPU warmup, set HPA scaleDown.stabilizationWindowSeconds >= 180 and prefer minReplicas >= 10 to avoid churn. We'll refine in postmortem.

support-bot: closing customer-facing notification as "mitigated".

eng-runtime-jay: capturing logs and metrics now for postmortem. Will attach analysis of kv-cache warmup times vs scale events.

matthew: timeline saved to incident doc. tagging oncall rotation for visibility.

maya (night-oncall): I'll mark this as monitored. If stable for next 2h, move to resolved and kick off PMs.

ops-danielle: thanks everyone. small follow-ups: check node kernel-driver patching schedule (possible fragmentation fix) and look at autoscaler rate-limiter options.

support-bot: Incident status: Mitigated -> Monitoring.

anya (oncall): end of handoff.
